newsitem.title: FINLAND: EMU to cut Finnish unemployment, hike wages - study.
newsitem.headline: EMU to cut Finnish unemployment, hike wages - study.

text.p: Finnish membership of the planned third stage of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would slightly reduce unemployment in the long run and raise real wages, according to a study released on Monday.
"EMU membership will slightly reduce unemployment in the long run," the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said in a statement.
"It will also raise real wages somewhat," ETLA said.
The study also found that "EMU will provide a more stable monetary environment and will probably also lower long-term reral interest rates," ETLA said.

"The increased effectiveness of fiscal policy due to stable interest rates will make dealing with recessions easier," it said, adding, however, that: "The potential disadvantage is that the ability to deal with domestic fluctuations may be too limited in EMU."
Competition would increase in domestic manufacturing and some services if Finland entered EMU, and export prospects would improve, ETLA said.
In EMU, wage differentials between firms and industries "will tend to grow, as competition for qualified labour and the international mobility of capital increase," the study showed.

ETLA said firm-specific solutions and profit-sharing should be used to achieve wage flexibility, but comprehensive collective bargaining could "play an important role" in order to "halt accelerating cost increases".
"Overall wage increases in EMU must remain very low," it said.
